body.prose:
Do tell me, where placing something freely on a dimension matters. I mean, we've been covering so many examples in OpenLight. We need a little bit of grounding here. To make a decision.

I don't know. It makes perfect sense that you can't manipulate someone else's knowledge. However, if you are standing on their knowledge, you ought to be able to see that others something connects to this one. And the other way around, if you are having your store reading from someone else's authored store, then you are the one who define your route and what matters most. And then you come out what you want, wherever you want. So for that, that's what I say. For many writers on a whole, well, if everything is flat, it's all about intersection, because then you are meeting a shit ton anyway. But the point of a reader is to kind of intersect for you if you're looking at the route. So there it would have to pull things together. Now, it makes perfect sense that every entry of some such information as a visit is collected into something. Now, you could do that with typed bodies, right? But again, it is not an append to place quite, is it? It's a have to update the whole on which types it. So it is a problem. So there you kind of want to place things. Into an existing collection.

I don't get what you're saying. If we are doing only typed, then of course I have to update the owner anytime I place a [holon]. Because I can't just place it with placement. I have to update the actual body of the place I'm placing it in.
body.title: Placing on a dimension
